name: Irena Digol
hero:
A personal approach

infertility
bio: Irena Digol was born in Chișinău and graduated from Nicolae Testemițanu State University of Medicine and Pharmacy in Moldova. In 2005, she defended her doctoral thesis on “Risk factors for cervical infection with oncogenic types of human papillomavirus”.

Author of research published in national and international medical journals, including the British Medical Journal and Contraception. She has collaborated with the Reproductive Health Training Centre and the National Centre for Health, Reproduction and Genetics at the Institute of Mother and Child in Moldova.

Participant in numerous international congresses and observerships in reproductive medicine, gynaecological oncology and gynaecological endocrinology in Europe and the USA. Since 2011, she has worked as a gynaecologist and fertility specialist at Terramed Medical Centre in Chișinău. Member of the European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology (ESHRE).
statement: According to current data, 10 to 20% of married couples are unable to conceive naturally.
factorsText:
Factors

1. Female age
As a woman ages, both the number and quality of her eggs gradually decline, reducing the likelihood of natural conception. The decline in fertility becomes more pronounced after 35 and accelerates considerably after 40. At the same time, the risk of chromosomal abnormalities in the embryo and pregnancy loss increases.

2. Ovulation disorders
Absent or irregular ovulation prevents natural conception. Common causes include polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), thyroid dysfunction, hyperprolactinaemia and other hormonal disorders. Many of these conditions can be diagnosed and treated.

3. Fallopian tube disorders
Blocked or damaged fallopian tubes prevent the egg and sperm from meeting. The main causes include previous pelvic inflammatory disease, sexually transmitted infections and the effects of surgery.

4. Endometriosis
Endometriosis can cause chronic inflammation, adhesions and changes to pelvic anatomy. Some forms of the condition reduce the likelihood of natural conception, particularly when the ovaries and fallopian tubes are affected. The impact depends on the extent and location of the disease.

5. Male factor
Changes in sperm count, motility or morphology can significantly reduce the likelihood of fertilisation. Causes include varicocele, hormonal and genetic disorders, infections and other conditions. An infertility assessment should therefore include both partners.
art: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) comprises medical technologies and diagnostic and treatment methods aimed at achieving pregnancy when some or all stages of conception take place outside the woman’s body.
ivf: IVF is a modern infertility treatment in which an egg is fertilised outside the woman’s body, in a laboratory.
The resulting embryos are transferred into the uterine cavity for further development. IVF is used when natural conception is difficult or impossible.
The method helps overcome many causes of infertility and significantly increases the likelihood of achieving a long-awaited pregnancy and the birth of a healthy child.
stepsText:
Steps

1. Preparing for the programme
Before IVF begins, the doctor assesses both partners’ reproductive health and determines the most appropriate treatment strategy. Investigations may include hormone tests, pelvic ultrasound, semen analysis and other tests as indicated. The results are used to develop an individual programme plan.

2. Stimulation and egg retrieval
Hormonal stimulation makes it possible to obtain several eggs in one cycle. Follicle growth is monitored by ultrasound and, when necessary, blood tests. When the follicles reach the required stage of development, the eggs are retrieved by ovarian puncture, usually under sedation.

3. Fertilisation and embryo development
The retrieved eggs are fertilised in the embryology laboratory using conventional IVF or ICSI. Over the following days, specialists monitor embryo development and assess embryo quality. Preimplantation genetic testing may be performed when indicated.

4. Embryo transfer
The selected embryo is transferred into the uterine cavity using a thin catheter, usually under ultrasound guidance. Transfer may take place in the current cycle or a later cycle after embryo cryopreservation. A blood hCG test is performed 9–14 days after transfer to determine whether pregnancy has occurred.

services.title: Assisted reproductive technology
services.body: Selecting an appropriate infertility treatment based on examination results and individual circumstances. Intrauterine insemination and in vitro fertilisation (IVF) are used when indicated to address difficulties with conception. Where necessary, we consider donor programmes and discuss every stage of treatment in detail.

services.title: Surgical approaches
services.body: The need for surgery and the choice of surgical method are determined after assessment and discussion of reproductive plans. Hysteroscopy allows examination of the uterine cavity and the necessary therapeutic procedures, while laparoscopy enables surgery on the pelvic organs through small incisions. Laparotomy is considered in situations requiring an open surgical approach.

services.title: Treatment of cervical conditions
services.body: Diagnosis and treatment of cervical conditions, including changes associated with human papillomavirus. Depending on the indications, assessment may include cervical cytology, HPV testing, colposcopy and biopsy. The results guide the choice of monitoring or treatment, taking into account the nature of the changes and reproductive plans.

services.title: Menopause concerns
services.body: Consultations on changes in well-being during the transition to menopause and after menopause. Selection of conservative treatment, including hormonal or non-hormonal methods when indicated, taking health status and possible contraindications into account.

faq.title: Can I choose my baby’s sex?
paragraphs: No. This is prohibited by law in Moldova and most countries. Although genetic testing can determine sex, using this information for sex selection is illegal.

faq.title: Is IVF advisable if there is a risk of genetic disease?
paragraphs: Yes. IVF with preimplantation diagnosis makes it possible to identify genetic conditions and transfer only healthy embryos.

faq.title: Do traditional remedies help with infertility?
paragraphs: There is no scientific evidence of their effectiveness. We use only methods recommended by international standards. Herbs and infusions are not prohibited, but they cannot replace evidence-based medicine.

faq.title: What is embryo freezing and why is it needed?
paragraphs: This is a cryopreservation protocol. After stimulation, we obtain several embryos, transfer 1–2 and freeze the others. This makes it possible to:
repeat the transfer without stimulation if the attempt is unsuccessful;
use the embryos for subsequent pregnancies.

faq.title: Does freezing reduce embryo quality?
paragraphs: No. Quality is preserved, although there is a small risk that some embryos may not survive thawing.
